description: 30 Form 4 theory questions for retrieval/marking benchmarks. Edit this file when testing a new subject or question set; pass --subject Biology|Chemistry|Physics to pick the textbook.

tests.label: Ch1 hypothesis full
tests.question: State the meaning of a hypothesis in a scientific investigation.
tests.studentAnswer: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation for an observation that can be tested by experiment.

tests.label: Ch1 variable partial
tests.question: State the difference between a manipulated variable and a responding variable.
tests.studentAnswer: One is changed and the other is what you measure.

tests.label: Ch1 hypothesis wrong
tests.question: State the meaning of a hypothesis in a scientific investigation.
tests.studentAnswer: A hypothesis is the proven conclusion after an experiment.

tests.label: Ch2 nucleus full
tests.question: State the function of the nucleus in a cell.
tests.studentAnswer: The nucleus controls all cell activities and contains genetic material in the form of DNA.

tests.label: Ch2 mitochondria partial
tests.question: State the function of mitochondria.
tests.studentAnswer: Mitochondria release energy for the cell.

tests.label: Ch2 nucleus wrong
tests.question: State the function of the nucleus in a cell.
tests.studentAnswer: The nucleus carries out photosynthesis to make food.

tests.label: Ch3 osmosis full
tests.question: Define osmosis.
tests.studentAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a partially permeable membrane.

tests.label: Ch3 osmosis partial
tests.question: Define osmosis.
tests.studentAnswer: Osmosis is when water moves through a membrane.

tests.label: Ch3 active transport wrong
tests.question: Explain active transport across the plasma membrane.
tests.studentAnswer: Active transport moves ions down a concentration gradient without using energy.

tests.label: Ch4 carbohydrate full
tests.question: State one function of carbohydrates in living organisms.
tests.studentAnswer: Carbohydrates provide energy for life processes and can be stored as glycogen or starch.

tests.label: Ch4 protein partial
tests.question: State one function of proteins in living organisms.
tests.studentAnswer: Proteins help the body grow.

tests.label: Ch4 lipid wrong
tests.question: State one function of lipids in living organisms.
tests.studentAnswer: Lipids speed up chemical reactions like enzymes.

tests.label: Ch5 enzyme def full
tests.question: Define an enzyme.
tests.studentAnswer: An enzyme is a protein that acts as a biological catalyst to speed up a chemical reaction without being changed.

tests.label: Ch5 enzyme temp partial
tests.question: Describe the effect of temperature on enzyme activity.
tests.studentAnswer: When temperature is too high, enzymes denature.

tests.label: Ch5 pineapple wrong
tests.question: A student adds pineapple juice to jelly but the jelly does not set. Explain why.
tests.studentAnswer: Pineapple is acidic so the jelly cannot set.

tests.label: Ch6 mitosis full
tests.question: State the importance of mitosis in living organisms.
tests.studentAnswer: Mitosis produces genetically identical daughter cells for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.

tests.label: Ch6 mitosis partial
tests.question: State the importance of mitosis in living organisms.
tests.studentAnswer: Mitosis is for growth of the body.

tests.label: Ch6 meiosis wrong
tests.question: State one difference between mitosis and meiosis.
tests.studentAnswer: Mitosis produces four haploid cells while meiosis produces two diploid cells.

tests.label: Ch7 aerobic full
tests.question: State the products of aerobic respiration in humans.
tests.studentAnswer: Carbon dioxide, water and energy.

tests.label: Ch7 aerobic partial
tests.question: State the products of aerobic respiration in humans.
tests.studentAnswer: Energy and carbon dioxide only.

tests.label: Ch7 anaerobic wrong
tests.question: State the product of anaerobic respiration in human muscles.
tests.studentAnswer: Ethanol and carbon dioxide.

tests.label: Ch9 bile full
tests.question: State the function of bile in digestion.
tests.studentAnswer: Bile emulsifies fats into smaller droplets to increase the surface area for lipase action.

tests.label: Ch9 pepsin partial
tests.question: State the function of pepsin in the stomach.
tests.studentAnswer: Pepsin digests proteins.

tests.label: Ch9 digestive wrong
tests.question: State where most absorption of digested food occurs.
tests.studentAnswer: In the stomach.

tests.label: Ch10 blood full
tests.question: State the function of red blood cells.
tests.studentAnswer: Red blood cells transport oxygen from the lungs to body tissues using haemoglobin.

tests.label: Ch10 circulation partial
tests.question: Explain double circulation in humans.
tests.studentAnswer: Blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit.

tests.label: Ch10 artery wrong
tests.question: State one structural difference between an artery and a vein.
tests.studentAnswer: Veins have thick muscular walls while arteries have thin walls.

tests.label: Ch11 antibody full
tests.question: Explain the role of antibodies in the immune response.
tests.studentAnswer: Antibodies are produced by lymphocytes and bind to antigens on pathogens to neutralise them or mark them for destruction.

tests.label: Ch12 reflex partial
tests.question: Explain what is meant by a reflex action.
tests.studentAnswer: A reflex is a quick automatic response.

tests.label: Ch14 fish tail full
tests.question: Explain how the tail of a fish helps in locomotion.
tests.studentAnswer: The tail fin moves sideways, pushing water backwards so the fish moves forward.
